title: Table S1.1. Validation of crossing heights against 28 documented passes.
note: Error is the GLO-30 crossing height of the matched col minus the reference elevation; it is computed for every pass but used only where a col lies within 5 km (Matched). Acceptance criterion, set before matching: median absolute error of 50 m or less and median bias within 30 m. Result: 18 of 28 passes matched, median absolute error 11 m, median bias -4 m, mean bias -28 m; with the alternative source, median absolute error 14 m.

title: Table S1.2. Published source of the reference elevation of the 28 documented passes, and whether each pass appears in Figure S1.2.
note: Full references are in Table S1.3. Passes not shown in Fig. S1.2 have no col within 5 km, so their published elevation was not compared. Each value was checked against the cited table or page. Pass coordinates come from the same INEI tables, except Anticona, Antajirca and the Chile-Argentina passes, whose coordinates are OpenStreetMap nodes. The alternative elevation of Anticona, 4818 m, is a commonly cited value that we could not trace to a publication. Weigend (2002) gives 2145 m for Porculla. Cristo Redentor and Túnel de Galera were excluded before matching, because their published elevations refer to a border complex and a tunnel, not to a col.

title: Table S1.3. Full references of the sources in Table S1.2.
note: The pages of the Unidad de Pasos Fronterizos carry no publication date. All URLs were last checked on 3 November 2026.

title: Table S1.4. Present montane gaps of the tropical divide (crossing height below 2000 m), from north to south.
note: Gaps are continuous runs of the crossing-height profile below the threshold. The 15 gaps add up to 210 km, and 4 of them are at least 10 km long. Level-1 unit: department, state or region within 500 m of the lowest point; the divide is often their boundary.

title: Table S1.5. The ten most isolated non-terminal tropical cols with depth of at least 100 m.
note: Isolation is the distance along the divide to the nearest lower point in each direction. Ranked by the smaller value. Every col is in APD_cols.csv.

title: Table S2.1. Sensitivity of the census to the depth threshold and to the gateway window.
note: Default: depth 100 m and window 100 km (both directions along the divide). Terminal cols and gateways are included in the counts.

title: Table S2.2. Sensitivity of the test of Janzen's prediction (GAM of thermal overlap on crossing height, absolute latitude and their interaction, with a smooth of position along the divide).
note: Janzen's prediction is a positive interaction. Indices on the 0-12 scale sum 12 monthly overlaps, so their coefficients are not comparable in size with those of the annual index. The all-cols model includes non-independent neighbouring cols and has residual spatial autocorrelation; it is shown only to compare the sign.

title: Table S2.3. Sensitivity of the montane gaps of the tropical divide to the threshold of montane climate.
note: Future values are the mean, minimum and maximum of the eight GCMs. Default threshold: 2000 m. Robust corridor loss under SSP3-7.0 in 2081-2100, critical gateways and share of the loss inside protected areas: 1500 m, 168.5 km, 5 gateways, 68%; 2000 m, 310.5 km, 6 gateways, 32%; 2500 m, 710.5 km, 10 gateways, 32%.

title: Table S2.4. Thermal overlap of the 61 non-terminal gateways, worse side, 1000 m flank, from north to south.
note: R is the annual range (bio5 - bio6) and d the shared length of the annual ranges of crest and flank, negative when they do not overlap, so that TOann = d / sqrt(R crest x R flank). Backup flank lists the sides where the descent path did not reach 1000 m within 150 km.

title: Table S2.5. Median crossing height, thermal overlap and flank temperature ranges of the 61 non-terminal gateways by zone and latitude band.
note: Medians of Table S2.4. A gateway has two sides, so 61 gateways have 122 sides.

title: Table S3.1. Typology of the 30 tropical gateways under the main rule and its three alternatives, and the side and direction of the aridity gap.
note: Main rule: thermal overlap at or above the median of the 30 tropical gateways is open in temperature; absolute aridity gap at or above the median is closed in moisture. Terciles: the middle third of either axis is intermediate. Each metric is that of the worse side (lower overlap, larger absolute gap); per-side gaps keep their sign, positive when the crest is wetter; the eastern side includes endorheic basins connected to the east.

title: Table S3.2. Number of tropical gateways of each type under the main rule and its alternatives.
note: The larger absolute aridity gap lies on the Pacific side at 22 of the 30 gateways, with the crest wetter than that flank, and on the eastern side at 8, with the crest drier than that flank.

title: Table S3.3. Moisture axis: Spearman correlations among the 30 tropical gateways and across the 61 gateways, and deviance of the GAMs.
note: Moisture gaps are the absolute values of the worse side. Terms of the GAMs are in Table 2a.

title: Table S4.1. Attributes of the 30 tropical gateways shown in the atlas.
note: Order from north to south. Flank route is the length of the steepest-descent path to 1000 m; 'Flank by nearest cell' lists the sides where the path did not reach 1000 m within 150 km. ΔT* is that of the worse side. Change in overlap: mean of the eight GCMs (range).

title: Table S5.1. The eight CMIP6 models used for future climates.
note: TCR and ECS from Hausfather et al. (2022), supporting data (Zelinka and IPCC AR6 Table 7.SM5; ECS from 150-year regressions). Filters, set before extracting any data: TCR within the AR6 likely range (1.4-2.2 °C) and ECS within the very likely range (2-5 °C); SSP1-2.6, SSP3-7.0 and SSP5-8.5 available in WorldClim 2.1; one model per institution or model family. Excluded by the last two filters: GFDL-ESM4 (no SSP5-8.5), ACCESS-CM2, AWI-CM-1-1-MR, GISS-E2-1-H, MIROC-ES2L and MPI-ESM1-2-LR.

title: Table S5.2. Future permeability of the 30 tropical gateways by GCM, scenario and period.
note: Future crest compared with the present flank, worse side; the precipitation gap is the larger absolute value of the two sides. ΔT* is the uniform warming that would centre the annual range of the crest on that of the present flank. No analogue: crest bio5 or bio6 beyond those of every present lowland cell below 1000 m within 100 km on the same side.
